precedents.deficiency_text:
3. We acknowledge your submission of data for the system suitability test for
resolution between impurity J and the drug substance. We however note that
there is not adequate resolution between impurities H, F and A. Perform the revalidation
of system suitability and demonstrate that there is adequate resolution between these impurities or alternatively, improve on your analytical method for
adequate resolution.

20. We note that you do not control for related compounds impurities A and B
(module 3.2.P.5.5, pages 5-7). This is not acceptable. We propose you provide
stability data for impurities A and B to demonstrate their absence in the finished
transdermal systems. Alternatively, revise the specification at release and
stability for the finished transdermal system to include tests and limits for these
impurities. Additionally, provide the analytical methods, method validation report
and COAs accordingly.

precedents.product_name:
Fentanyl Transdermal System,
 12.5 mcg/hr, 25 mcg/hr, 50 mcg/hr, 75 mcg/hr and 100 mcg/hr.
precedents.deficiency_text:
2. We have the following recommendations for your leachables study. 

a. Identify all the impurities from the release liner, backing layer, and ink that could potentially leach into the drug product. Using reference standards for these identified impurities, demonstrate that the analytical methods are capable of detecting these impurities in the drug product at the desired level. 

b. We acknowledge that you plan to conduct a second leachables study on the newly manufactured post-ANDA batches with all of the changes (ink, release liner, and pouch stock) implemented. Please submit the results. You are encouraged to provide a multiple time point leachable analysis (e.g. 0, 6, 12, 24 months) to provide the most robust understanding of the leachable profile. In addition, we recommend that your analytical evaluation threshold be calculated based on a safety concern threshold of 1.5 mcg/day and a maximum daily dose of three 100-mcg/hr fentanyl transdermal systems.
